raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview Fixes #64275. With adaptive verification enabled, startup can run out of GPU memory in the cost-profiling loop of `capture_model()`, which runs after the KV cache is allocated. The loop profiles shapes in ascending size and keeps the allocator cache until it finishes, so the cache grows to the sum of all shapes. This PR releases the cache whenever the profiled batch changes, so the cache holds at most one shape at a time. ## Claims - DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on 4x MI355X at `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.95` now starts and serves. On main, it aborts with `HSA_STATUS_ERROR_OUT_OF_RESOURCES`. - KV cache size and startup time are unchanged. Fixed-K and no-speculation paths are untouched. ## Validation All runs used `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-edad8b03c5285a1c12e7e4f83c1af709b319a01b`, with this PR's `model_runner.py` mounted over it for the "this PR" column. Model: `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017@1bae0e10`, 4x MI355X, TP4 + EP. ```bash VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ADAPTIVE_VERIFICATION_PROFILE_CONTEXT_LEN=4096 \ vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 --tensor-parallel-size 4 \ --enable-expert-parallel --gpu-memory-utilization 0.95 \ --max-num-seqs 512 --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 \ --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":5,"enable_adaptive_verification":true}' ``` | `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.95` | main | this PR | |---|---|---| | Startup | OOM in cost profiling (4/4 ranks) | ready | | KV cache memory per rank | 174.34 GiB | 174.34 GiB | | Engine init | 318 s (at 0.90, where main starts) | 318 s | | `vllm bench serve`, random 512/128, 256 prompts, concurrency 64 | — | 256/256 OK | | Same load, fixed K=5 (adaptive off) | — | 256/256 OK | | Same load, no speculation | — | 256/256 OK | Unit tests: ```bash pytest tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner_v2.py \ tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner_v2_cudagraph_profiling.py \ tests/v1/spec_decode/test_adaptive_verification.py # ROCm (MI355X): 60 passed, 1 skipped (requires CUDA) ``` The new `test_capture_model_bounds_adaptive_verification_profiling_cache` fails on main: ```text > assert peak_cached == max(sizes) << 30 E assert 7516192768 == (4 << 30) ``` It uses this file's existing `_make_capture_runner` harness, the same one the #61509 and #63431 tests use. A real-allocator test would need a model large enough to exhaust device memory after KV-cache allocation, so the end-to-end run above is the real-path check.
Root-cause diagnostics (temporary instrumentation on the earlier nightly c50aca144) Allocator stats on rank 0, logged after every profiling run by a temporary debug build. The right column adds this PR's fix. | | main @ 0.90 | with this PR's fix @ 0.95 | |---|---:|---:| | Free memory when profiling starts | 22.24 GiB | 7.62 GiB | | Reserved growth over the loop | 24.88 GiB | 5.29 GiB | | Largest live allocation of any shape | 2.51 GiB | 2.50 GiB | | Minimum free memory during the loop | 0.42 GiB | 2.30 GiB | Calibrated cost curves, main vs this PR's fix (one run each): both runs measured the draft curve at the same 53 batch sizes (median difference 0.4%, max 1.1%) and the verify curve at the same 58 (median 1.0%, max 2.3%).
## Details **Root cause.** `batches_to_profile()` yields every captured size, then the eager tail sizes, in ascending order, with five replays each. Each larger shape needs bigger blocks than any cached one, so the cache grows by about one shape per size until the device is full. The final failing allocation belongs to the HIP runtime, so PyTorch's free-and-retry cannot help. #61509 empties the cache only after the loop. **Why release on batch change.** - It bounds the cache to one shape without changing profile order or KV sizing. That shape (at most 2.5 GiB here) fits in the activation headroom that KV sizing already reserves. - The release happens outside the timed region. - Comparing the whole batch keeps the release correct if profiling gains more axes, as in #62960. - Profiling in descending order also starts, but it leaves less margin and relies on allocator block splitting. **Not a duplicate.** - #61509 and #63154 (merged) release memory only after the loop. - #63431 (merged) and #56182 change only the pre-KV pass. - #63410 conflicts on one line, but not semantically. **Limitations.** - Validated on ROCm only. The change is platform-neutral (`torch.accelerator.empty_cache()`). - The reproduction sets `VLLM_ADAPTIVE_VERIFICATION_PROFILE_CONTEXT_LEN=4096` to avoid a separate ROCm fault at the default of 8192. AI assistance was used for the investigation and this change. The submitter has reviewed every changed line. ---
Pull Request Checklist - [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans). - [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR. - [x] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity. - [x] **Testing and Validation:** Validates the change and ensures any added tests are meaningful and reliable, with CI coverage or documented CI resource constraints and validation performed outside CI. - [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples. - [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes a brief summary and relevant links, supports claims with evidence, explains root causes and implementation trade-offs, and follows the contributing guide.

> **Question**: Did we consider iterating through the batch sizes in reverse order as an alternative fix (descending in size)? Might be less intrusive vs running `torch.accelerator.empty_cache()`

Good question, yes, I tested descending order. It also starts at 0.95, but the minimum free memory during profiling was 1.06 GiB vs 2.30 GiB with this PR (the smaller shapes fragment the large cached blocks), and it relies on the allocator splitting those blocks rather than explicitly bounding the cache. Releasing on batch change also stays correct if profile batches gain more axes (e.g. #62960), where "descending" isn't well defined. The cost is ~57 empty_cache() calls at startup with no measurable effect on startup time.
@tuukkjs thanks for the PR! This looks like a clean and minimal fix.

@@ -481,6 +481,50 @@ def _dummy_run(num_tokens):
     assert curves == ([] if profile_only else [[]])
 
 
+def test_capture_model_bounds_adaptive_verification_profiling_cache(monkeypatch):
+    """Adaptive verification profiles shapes in ascending size after the KV
+    cache is allocated. A larger shape cannot reuse the blocks a smaller one
+    left cached, so without a release between shapes the cache grows to the
+    sum of every shape's activations instead of the largest one's."""
+    runner = _make_capture_runner(monkeypatch, captured=True)
+    sizes = [1, 2, 4]
+    monkeypatch.setattr(
+        runner.cudagraph_manager, "captured_token_counts", lambda: sizes, raising=False
+    )
+    runner.step_timing = SimpleNamespace(collect=lambda: contextlib.nullcontext([]))
+    runner.adaptive_verification = SimpleNamespace(
+        batches_to_profile=lambda sizes: [
+            {"num_tokens": n} for n in sizes for _ in range(2)
+        ],
+        set_initial_cost_curves=lambda timings: None,
+    )
+    # Cached bytes per shape: a shape reuses only its own blocks.
+    cached: dict[int, int] = {}
+    profiled: list[int] = []
+    peak_cached = 0
+
+    def _dummy_run(num_tokens):
+        nonlocal peak_cached
+        cached[num_tokens] = num_tokens << 30
+        profiled.append(num_tokens)
+        peak_cached = max(peak_cached, sum(cached.values()))
+
+    monkeypatch.setattr(runner, "_dummy_run", _dummy_run)
+    monkeypatch.setattr(
+        model_runner_module, "freeze_gc_for_cudagraph_capture", contextlib.nullcontext
+    )
+    monkeypatch.setattr(torch.accelerator, "empty_cache", cached.clear)
+    monkeypatch.setattr(
+        torch.accelerator, "get_memory_info", lambda: (16 << 30, 16 << 30)
+    )
+    monkeypatch.setattr(model_runner_module, "lock_workspace", lambda: None)
+
+    runner.capture_model()
+
+    assert profiled == [1, 1, 2, 2, 4, 4]
+    assert peak_cached == max(sizes) << 30
+
+
